answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond in a vault and gets a kernel seed bound to its vault key. Each epoch it publishes the sequence that kernel generates. An auditor recomputes any sequence from the public kernel table; a mismatch, reused seed, or shared vault key burns the bond. The first filing costs 36 credits, the kth 36+8(k-1), so the 1000th costs 8028 and 1000 fakes cost 4032000 plus 70000 locked. A rented-kernel ring fails: its identities emit identical sequences, seen as one plume of copies, and every bond in it burns. An honest agent pays 36 once and recovers it after a clean epoch.
